content:
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience role. I am a Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology with hands-on experience building accessible web applications in React and TypeScript, including a software development internship at Harbourline Media and a full-stack academic project.

At Harbourline Media, I worked on accessibility fixes for a React news site and built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages. I documented the component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library. In my Tidewatch final-year project, I developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js and Express API, with PostgreSQL for user favourites. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. These experiences connect closely with your focus on accessible patient-facing features, Node.js services, PostgreSQL and automated testing.

I am drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare software straightforward and human-centered. The opportunity to build features that help people book visits and manage follow-up care is meaningful to me, and I value your emphasis on accessibility and privacy. I would be glad to bring my practical web development experience and commitment to accessible user experiences to your Patient Experience squad while continuing to grow as an engineer.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Verdane Care.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured, and clearly tailored to Verdane Care's Patient Experience role. It uses specific evidence from the Harbourline Media internship and Tidewatch project rather than relying on generic claims. The accessibility focus, technical stack, testing tools, and PostgreSQL experience are communicated effectively. The motivation paragraph also reflects the company's patient-first, human-centered positioning without making unsupported claims. The main content opportunity is to include one additional relevant project detail that strengthens the wellness-domain connection.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS- and parsing-friendly: it uses standard headings and paragraphs, contains no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting, and includes relevant terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, accessibility, screen readers, and Lighthouse. AI screening probability is moderate to high for keyword relevance, but likely reduced for this specific role because the document does not demonstrate the required two years of professional React/TypeScript experience and does not mention Git, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or web security fundamentals. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than formatting defects, and unsupported terms should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with accessible patient-facing web experiences, React and TypeScript frontend development, Node.js and Express services, PostgreSQL, automated unit testing, Storybook, and a user-focused approach. The Tidewatch project provides particularly relevant evidence of accessibility testing with NVDA and VoiceOver and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The cover letter also aligns well with Verdane Care's emphasis on patients first, privacy, accessibility, and straightforward human-centered software. The candidate's material shows a gap against the 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience requirement: the documented professional internship lasted approximately four months, while the remaining work is academic or freelance. It also does not establish Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, OWASP/web-security awareness, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, healthcare experience, AWS, Docker, German/Croatian, or analytics/A/B testing. The yoga-studio project does provide relevant wellness-domain experience but is currently omitted from the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT: In the second paragraph, after the Tidewatch evidence, add one concise sentence about the freelance yoga-studio project to show the candidate's relevant wellness experience without overstating it. For example: "My freelance Next.js project for a yoga studio also gave me experience building a user-facing wellness website with a class timetable and email-based booking requests." Keep the existing accessibility and technical evidence, and do not claim healthcare, regulated-environment, GDPR, Git, end-to-end testing, or security experience that is not supported by the candidate information.

PRECISION IMPROVEMENT: In the final sentence of the second paragraph, change "automated testing" to "automated unit testing" or "Jest-based testing" because the candidate information supports Jest and React Testing Library but does not document end-to-end testing. For example, change "These experiences connect closely with your focus on accessible patient-facing features, Node.js services, PostgreSQL and automated testing" to "These experiences connect closely with your focus on accessible patient-facing features, Node.js services, PostgreSQL and automated unit testing."

I am a Computing student at Liffey Institute of Technology with hands-on experience building accessible web applications in React and TypeScript, including a software development internship at Harbourline Media and a full-stack academic project.

At Harbourline Media, I worked on accessibility fixes for a React news site and built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages. I documented the component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library. In my Tidewatch final-year project, I developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js and Express API, with PostgreSQL for user favourites. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. My freelance Next.js project for a yoga studio also gave me experience building a user-facing wellness website with a class timetable and email-based booking requests. These experiences connect closely with your focus on accessible patient-facing features, Node.js services, PostgreSQL and automated unit testing.

I am drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare software straightforward and human-centered. The opportunity to build features that help people book visits and manage follow-up care is meaningful to me, and I value your emphasis on accessibility and privacy. I would be glad to bring my practical web development experience and commitment to accessible user experiences to your Patient Experience squad while continuing to grow as an engineer.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Verdane Care.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise cover letter with a clear opening, relevant evidence, and a professional closing. It presents the candidate's strongest truthful matches: React and TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, and wellness-related freelance work. The examples are specific and credible, particularly the screen-reader-friendly gallery and Tidewatch's Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The main content limitation is that the letter does not mention the teaching assistant experience, which could support the role's mentoring expectation. It also relies on general statements about privacy and patient-facing work rather than directly connecting the candidate's existing experience to responsible handling of user data.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional punctuation, readable paragraphs, and many exact job-description keywords, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library. AI screening probability is good for a junior or early-career profile because the evidence is concrete and consistent with the associated CV. Screening probability for this specific role may be reduced by the absence of explicit terms such as semantic HTML, responsive layouts, Git, web security fundamentals, OWASP Top 10, integration testing, and end-to-end testing. These should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information. The letter also does not state the candidate's level of experience in a way that could help a reviewer correctly interpret the application, although it does accurately identify the internship and academic project.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's accessibility focus, React/TypeScript frontend work, Node.js and PostgreSQL project experience, automated testing with Jest, Storybook, and the company's wellness and human-centred context. The yoga studio project is a relevant truthful connection to the wellness domain. It also reflects the company's patient-first and straightforward-software themes without making unsupported claims of healthcare experience. However, the candidate does not meet the stated 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience: the available material shows a four-month internship and freelance/project work. The candidate material also does not establish Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP/web-security awareness beyond use of Firebase Authentication, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, analytics/A/B testing, or healthcare/regulated-environment experience. The letter appropriately avoids claiming these gaps as strengths. The teaching assistant experience is relevant to the role's mentoring expectation but is currently omitted.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, after the sentence ending "automated unit testing," add one truthful sentence showing the mentoring experience: "As a teaching assistant for a first-year web development lab, I also supported approximately 30 students during a semester of lab sessions." This strengthens alignment with the role's expectation to mentor interns or junior colleagues without overstating the experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the first paragraph, change "including a software development internship at Harbourline Media and a full-stack academic project" to "including a software development internship at Harbourline Media, a full-stack final-year project, and a freelance Next.js website." This gives the reader a faster, more complete overview of the candidate's evidence and uses the job-relevant Next.js term earlier.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the final paragraph, replace "practical web development experience" with "practical React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and accessibility experience." This makes the closing more keyword-specific while remaining fully supported by the candidate information.
